utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Good morning; good morning, everybody. We have reconvened today in order to try to bring this hearing to the end, and we will be hearing the rejoinder of the Defence this week. Before we bring in the witness, the Chamber should like to have some clarification from the parties, namely, some additional information about the witnesses that have been proposed, the witnesses for Mr. Kvocka and also the witnesses that have been proposed for Mr. Prcac. The issue seems to be very simple and clear, and we should like to hear an equally simple and clear answer. What testimony or, rather, what witnesses and facts that will be discussed during the testimony which will be heard as part of the rejoinder of the -- which have arisen from the rebuttal of the Prosecutor is the testimony that the Defence wishes to propose? I'm asking this question of Mr. Krstan Simic first of all, and Mr. Jovan Simic, and then we will be hearing the Prosecutor, that is to say, about what facts arising from the Prosecution case will be discussed during the rejoinder.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. As you have said, we have announced two witnesses which we propose to hear about facts that have been discussed by Witness AW before this Chamber. Witness Jasminka Kvocka participated in this incident. She was present there. She even made coffee after they came back from the first visit. She knows about the garage and everything else. And it was impossible for us to examine this witness about the circumstances for the simple reason because the testimony and the statement of Witness AW was not disclosed at the time. So we didn't have any indication, any information as to the importance of these facts. And the same goes for Mr. Kvocka. During his cross-examination, Mr. Kvocka was examined about the said events, and he indeed confirmed his participation in this event, but as we didn't have the statement of Witness AW, we didn't have an opportunity to examine Mr. Kvocka about this particular incident, neither did we have an opportunity to carry out our own investigation which would provide us with the appropriate basis for the examination. For those reasons, we believe that it is in the interests of justice for these two witnesses to be heard, because we were not in a position to know what would be discussed by this particular witness during the rebuttal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Simic, if we bear in mind the entire story of the case, that is, the visit to the locality, what those individuals did there and what they did afterwards with what they had found, so if we bear these three aspects of the event in the mind, what are the things that you wish to contest?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, we contest that there was -- that Mr. Kvocka took any part of that loot. After Mr. Momcilo Gruban begged Mr. Kvocka, and since Mr. Gruban was his friend and since -- and Witness AW confirmed that, he was his employee, they had contacts later on. Mr. AW had an intention to leave the area, and he had contact to that effect with the Ministry of the Interior, and he said to Mr. Gruban that he would give him his apartment, and in the end he didn't do that and that is the reason why he didn't say goodbye to Mr. Momcilo Gruban, and there are so many similar elements to that effect, and we wish to say that -- we wish to show that Mr. Kvocka wanted to help both upon the insistence of his wife. And in particular, we want to contest the participation of the sister of Mr. AW in the said events. Nobody else saw that woman, and we will try to prove that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Krstan Simic, for this clarification. You may be seated now, and I will give the floor to Mr. Jovan Simic with the same question; that is to say, what is the testimony and who are the witnesses and the facts which were presented by the Prosecutor which you intend to contest in your rejoinder with your four proposed witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. First of all, I should like to inform the Chamber that one witness has not arrived. Nedja Karalic hasn't come here. He has had heart surgery and his doctor has not allowed him to fly. That is why he -- we have been left with three witnesses who have arrived here, and they will be testifying about three facts. First of all, that Mr. -- about two facts. First of all, that Mr. Prcac, during the month of June, was and worked in the police station department Omarska and not in the camp as was testified by Witness Karalic. The second fact which we intend to contest was the incident involving the gun dragging, that is that Mr. Prcac pulled a gun and aimed it at the guards of the Omarska camp, which was testified -- which was denied by Witness Karalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much, Mr. Jovan Simic. Ms. Somers, let us hear you. In view of the information that has just been supplied by the Defence counsel, what exactly is your position?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all, as to Jasminka Kvocka's being or not being, there was cross-examination on this matter. There is nothing to have suggested from any extracts that were provided, pursuant to the events of the week of the 28th, that Mrs. Kvocka was anywhere near there. There's no testimony she was there. I believe that we may be receiving potentially fabricated evidence. The degree to which Witness AW was cross-examined was quite thorough, and there was simply no mention of the presence of another woman other than the sibling. Further, the cross-examination of Kvocka itself on this point was quite thorough and the redirect, during which time this issue could have been raised, Kvocka didn't volunteer that his wife was present. And suddenly, a new witness appears which, at the very least, is suspicious and, at the potential outside, is not going to be true testimony. Our written submissions, I think, cover the bases for it. If the Chamber is minded to hear Jasminka Kvocka because her testimony did not have included in it anything about this, which is normal because there was no information and we have reason to believe that it is not even germane to her, that she was not involved, then we'd have to leave that in the Chamber's hands. We did not argue in our written submissions her exclusion. However, as to Miroslav Kvocka, he had fully the floor on this issue, the facts within his own knowledge. If he or his attorney chose to withhold discussing those during their case, that is a strategic decision made by them. To abuse rejoinder now, to come back and remedy perhaps a poor strategic decision, is an abuse of the entire process. On the issues of the witnesses for Mr. Prcac, we've set forth that practically every aspect that was raised about criminal technician was raised and properly belonged in the case in chief for Mr. Prcac. It was covered adequately. This is perhaps a second bite at the apple, trying to get in some either mitigation evidence which does not belong in this phase. The cumulative nature of it suggests, if consistent with the Court's practices, that it would not be helpful to the Chamber. The substance does not offer anything that the Chamber has not heard during the case in chief. The challenge to the issue of the weapon or not, it's really a case of raised in rebuttal -- raised by the Defence for the first time, challenged in rebuttal, and there's really nothing new to hear about it. It's going to be denial -- there was a denial by the affected detainee as to the occurrence. It seems that there would be nothing additional to add that could not have been brought out on cross-examination. The issue of mood of the community was not raised during the rebuttal case and does not properly belong here. If there is some type of discussion about sympathising or whatever, that may have been suggested during the Defence case, it was not pursued at all during rebuttal and I think has no place during this week's testimony. These are matters that simply did not arise during the course of the rebuttal case. As the Chamber -- we, of course, are taking great pains to read this Chamber's rulings on what is the appropriate type of proof for rebuttal and rejoinder, and we find that these are outside of the Chamber's own rulings. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Ms. Somers, can I ask you what's your position. Mr. Simic said that one of the rebuttal aspects for Mr. Prcac would be that during June he wasn't in Omarska, he was in the police station. That's what he just said a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Sorry. I'm just checking. I was passed a note. The issue of whether or not he was officially in Omarska, Your Honour, is absolutely irrelevant. Whether he was there officially on duty or had access as a police officer, whether his duties at Omarska had commenced officially or not, we think is not the point. It is his position which later did transfer to Omarska that is relevant, and witness Kugic never said that he was working there at the time. There's no proof that was adduced about working there or not as to that particular incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Let me make sure I understand you. You're saying that the Prosecution isn't maintaining that he had any functioning position in Omarska during June?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Our position is that he took over from Kvocka officially, and the dates are not necessarily firmly -- I think that there is room for argument, which we will put forth in our submissions, about who actually left and whether or not one officially had to be there to carry on certain duties, whether de facto or de jure. There is evidence that Prcac had been in the camp even prior to any time that he may have officially replaced Kvocka as, according to the Prosecution's case, deputy commander. And the fact that he was nonetheless attached to the Omarska Police Station, giving him the authority to get in the camp, is significant. So his exercise of authority in one way or the other is present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: That's good argument, but I'm not sure you made the case for its irrelevance.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: In terms of -- for purposes of his being in the camp, Kugic, if I am correct, said that he was acting personally, not officially, if I recall the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, if I may just add: And even in that capacity, whether he was officially assigned, trying to extort money was still very much on his agenda, and that was the point. But my recollection is that Kugic did not indicate that he was doing it in official capacity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us just see whether Mr. Krstan Simic has anything to add, and then later on I'll give the floor to Mr. Jovan Simic. If yes, please be brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will be very brief, indeed. We have asked the witness about Mrs. Kvocka, about the car and the garage, so there are a number of relevant things that still need to be clarified. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jovan Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I, too, will be very brief. The Defence suggests that during the presentation of the case, we tried to show that Mr. Prcac arrived to his working place on the 15th of July, 1992, that is, that he came to the investigation centre in Omarska on that day. Prior to that day, he did not have any official capacity there, nor was any evidence led to that effect. Mr. Kugic, during his rebuttal testimony, stated that during the night, that is, during the shift that he was on while he was on duty, Mr. Prcac came down and he spent the whole night with him. What is important here was that he had a function there, that he was working at the investigation centre. I hope that there is enough evidence that Mr. Prcac, prior to the 15th of July, did not come to work at the investigation centre in Omarska. Once again, we are trying to lead evidence to prove that Mr. Prcac, in the month of June, up until the 15th of July, was assigned to the Omarska Police Station Department as a reserve policeman and that he was working there as a crime technician. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe we have finished, Ms. Somers. Is there something new that you wish to inform us about?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: No. Just emphasis that there was never any testimony about his being on duty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Let me consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber is now going to make its ruling. The Chamber has received the list of witnesses that the accused Mr. Kvocka and Mr. Prcac propose to call in rejoinder for this week, and it has also received the response of the Prosecutor in which the Prosecutor expressed its opposition to the calling of the witnesses that have been mentioned. The Defence of Mr. Kvocka wishes to call Mrs. Jasminka Kvocka and Mr. Kvocka, who are supposed to testify about the details of the testimony of Witness AW, who was called by the Prosecutor during its case in rebuttal. The Prosecutor opposes the testimony of the accused Mr. Kvocka because he, as they put it, has already had an opportunity to pronounce himself about the incident with Witness AW during his cross-examination. The Defence of the accused Mr. Prcac wishes to call four witnesses, and they have informed the Chamber today that Witness Nedja Karalic will not be present here. The Prosecution opposes these witnesses because the subject matter of their testimonies does not arise from evidence which was presented by the Prosecutor during his case in rebuttal. The Chamber wishes to remind the parties that it applies the test from the Celebici judgement, which was done in the case of the rebuttal of the Prosecutor. The test is as follows: The Defence case will not be admitted in rejoinder -- will be admitted in rejoinder only if it is pertinent and if it arises from the evidence which was called by the Prosecutor during his case in rebuttal, and that is why the elements which concern a key aspect of the Defence case will not be admitted. The Chamber believes that although the accused Mr. Kvocka has had an opportunity to testify about the incident which was testified about by Witness AW during his cross-examination, the Witness AW presented certain new elements. Generally speaking, this witness has supplied the Chamber with certain details concerning the contact between the witness and Mr. Kvocka and Mr. Gruban about how they met and how they first went to the house in Carakovo. He also spoke about the work which was done at the house in Carakovo, the return of the Grubans to Pecani and the threats that were expressed by Mr. Kvocka; furthermore, about the second attempt which took place the following day and also what was done with the jewelry which was dug out that day and also the third visit to the house on the following day. The Chamber believes that the response of Mr. Kvocka to new elements which were presented by Witness AW falls within the scope of the rejoinder. The same argument, the same reasoning, is applied to the testimony of Mrs. Kvocka about the same subject. As regards the witnesses that have been proposed by the accused Mr. Prcac, the Chamber considers that the facts which surround the issue of the police station department in Omarska and the investigation centre in Omarska and also the incident involving the gun dragging in Omarska also fall within the scope of rejoinder of the Defence. Therefore, the Chamber will authorise the testimony of the witnesses that have been proposed by the Defence of the accused Mr. Kvocka and Mr. Prcac. These witnesses will testify as rejoinder witnesses during this week. The Chamber has rendered its ruling, and I think that we are now ready, Mr. Krstan Simic, to proceed. You have the floor, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The Defence now calls witness Jasminka Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mrs. Jasminka Kvocka. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are back in the Tribunal once again. You have already taken the solemn declaration before this Trial Chamber, and we're going to consider your testimony as a continuation of your previous testimony and the oath and solemn declaration you took on that occasion. So you are continuing your testimony under the solemn declaration you made the first time you were here. Do you accept that? Are you fully conscious of the fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Then you may be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will first be answering questions put to you by Mr. Simic. Mr. Simic, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. In view of the fact that you have resolved the dilemma and take this to be a continuation of the testimony, we're not going to ask the witness her particulars, but we'll resume the examination where we left off.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mrs. Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you know somebody by the name of Momcilo Gruban, nicknamed Ckalja?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Since when have you known that individual?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I have known him for many years.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Where do you know him from?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: My husband and that man are from the same village. They were born in the same village.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Were they friends?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. They were friends for a long time. They knew each other, and their two families have a relationship of kumship. They are kum to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Gruban ask you or your husband for any assistance in the course of 1993?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what that was all about?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Sometimes I would ask Mr. Gruban for help and assistance and sometimes he would ask me for some help or assistance, or my husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Now, when he asked you for your help, what was that about? Was there any problem?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: They came -- he came to our apartment on one occasion, and he wanted our help and assistance for a friend of us. He wanted us to do a favour. This man had done him a favour. Whether he was his foreman or whether he had taken him on and given him a job, they worked in the same work organisation and he wanted to return the favour.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did he say in actual fact what the assistance was, what kind of help he wanted you to give this friend of his?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. We were sitting around my place, and they were talking about the fact that something had been left of his sister's and that something had to be found in order for Gruban to be able to leave Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, was any mention made of the fact that Gruban's friend had tabled a request to leave the police force?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: And what were your husband's reactions to that?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't know what to say really. My husband couldn't tell anybody whether to leave or to stay. It's a personal decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask you about the decision made by Mr. Gruban's friend. What I asked you was what were your husband's reactions at this request made by Mr. Gruban to have him help his friend?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, he didn't actually want to help his friend, because when Gruban's -- when we heard what Gruban's friend was supposed to do, what you had to do was to have a car first to go to the village and then to have the things to get this done with. We didn't have any of that because we lived in the apartment building that we lived in.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: So was everything over during this one conversation or were there other visits and conversations?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, Gruban came by several times. But what we needed was to secure a vehicle, a car to go there. We had to decide and see who we were going to borrow a car from, because we didn't have a car ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, as we're on this subject, you say that you did not have a car. To make things clearer, could you tell us whether you and your husband owned a passenger car in the course of 1992, 1993, or 1994?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Are passenger vehicles registered at the police station in the name of their owners?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. There is a special service for vehicle registration.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we should like to tender into evidence at this point the following document: I think that the number is D1/53A and B, and it is a certificate issued by the Public Security Centre of Prijedor. The number is 14-03/1-1-222-41, dated the 13th of June, 2001, from which it emerges that Mr. Kvocka and his wife were not the owners of any passenger vehicle in the course of 1992, 1993, and 1994. I should like to tender this document into evidence, and I have supplied copies of the document for all the parties and for the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Krystal, that is to say, the registrar, draws my attention to the fact that there might have been an error in the numbering of this document. Madam Registrar, you have the floor to explain.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. The next number for the Exhibit is D1/54 instead of D1/53. D1/53 has already been tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I stand corrected. It was my mistake. I repeated the previous number. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, very well. Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Krstan Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, while we're on the subject of the ownership of cars, could you tell us, please, whether you or your husband owned a garage in Prijedor in your apartment building.

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you ever own a garage?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you own a garage today?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, here and now the Defence would also like to substantiate Mrs. Kvocka's testimony by showing two documents. The first is a certificate of the property service keeping records of real estate and property of the Prijedor municipality. The number is 35-952-141/01. The date is the 11th of June, 2001. From this document, it can be seen that Mrs. Jasminka Kvocka, nee Crnalic, does not possess any real estate in the territory of Prijedor municipality. This document would now be D1/55A and B, I believe. I should like at the same time, under the following number, 35-952-142/01, dated the 11th of June, 2001, a document issued by the same body, testifying to the fact that Miroslav Kvocka, son of Dragomir, does not possess any real estate or garage of the kind testified to by Witness AW. So I should like to tender those two documents into evidence and hand them over.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, just briefly tell us what kind of building you live in.

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I live in the Pecani settlement. It is an apartment building with five entrances.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What floor do you live on?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: The second floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Have you got a garden of any kind?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you have any need to have a shovel and pick in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, of course not. Where would I keep such things?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, you said a moment ago -- let me restate that. When did your husband decide to help Ckalja and Ckalja's friend? When did he make that decision?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, they would come for several days to the apartment and discuss the matter. The weather was poor, was bad weather, and this man, Ckalja's friend -- that is to say, Ckalja felt that he had to return a favour because the man had given him a job.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you, when was this decision made? When did you make the decision to help the man?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Do you want the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: No, not the exact date. Just tell us approximately. Can you tell us the month?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say the exact month. But they spent several days discussing the matter and how this could be done, because I said we didn't have a car. So he would come every other day. He would come to see how this could be done. Miro didn't actually want to do this because he had to go to work the next day. Perhaps it was at my insistence, I wanted to go with them and help them. Very often I didn't -- I went with my husband. I didn't like him going off on his own. But we had some guests, and it was at my insistence. I sort of forced him to help the man and go, to help Gruban, because I too had to repay a debt. I owed Gruban something because I sent my brother's packages through Gruban. So I wanted to return the favour and to help his friend by the same token.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You said you didn't have a car. So what did you do about the car? How did you resolve that problem?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: We asked Hasan Oklopcic, a friend of ours, to lend us a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you obtain the car? Did your husband obtain the car?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, what did you do about the shovel and pick?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: They didn't know what they would use to dig the stuff up, and I said that my brothers and my parents' house -- in my parents' house, that there was a shovel and a pick and that they could go and borrow that, because my parents cultivate a small portion of land.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you call anybody up in that regard?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I called my brothers up and said that Miro, my husband, together with Ckalja, would come by to pick up the shovel and pick.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Which brother did you talk to?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I talked to my brother Rizak.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: When they returned, did they come back to your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, they came back to my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who came to your apartment on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: My husband, Ckalja, and Ckalja's friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: And was that the first time you saw Ckalja's friend?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you know him from before?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What did you talk about? Were you present throughout the conversation?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, what did they talk about?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: While I was making coffee and getting some drinks for them, they said that they hadn't succeeded in doing what they had set out to do and that they would go on another occasion, because he said he had to call his sister abroad for her to explain exactly where it was all located. He wasn't able to find his way around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, did they go a second time?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: When did they go this second time? How much time elapsed from the first time to the second time?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: They went three or four days later. Perhaps it was a week later or maybe it was two weeks later. I don't know exactly. But several days went by.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: They didn't go the next day?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. The next day, my husband went off to work and Ckalja had some of his own duties to see to, so they weren't able to go the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: After they went the second time, did they come back to your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did your husband tell you anything about how the whole, if I can call it, operation ended?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: He said they had done nothing, managed to do nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the second time.

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. The second time he said that they had found something, a jar or a box, but not anything very much. They didn't find what Ckalja's friend had expected to find, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether they went again later on?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: While you were drinking coffee in your apartment, what was the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. atmosphere like? What was the general mood and the relationship between Ckalja and his friend?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, they talked about the apartment of Ckalja's friend, and he said that when he signed off from Prijedor, he would go to Germany and leave Ckalja his apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: But were they friendly, on friendly terms or not friendly terms?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, it couldn't have been not friendly, because they had been friends for so many years and worked together. So it was necessarily friendly. It couldn't have been unfriendly. In my house, nobody ever felt unfriendly towards each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, you said a moment ago that Mr. Gruban told you that his friend had signed off and that he was going abroad and that that's why he had to get this job done and that he needed assistance for it.

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to tender another exhibit into evidence. It is a certificate from the Public Security Centre of Prijedor. The number is 14-03/1-1-207/20-410, dated the 5th of June, 2001. And for protective measures for the witness, I should just like to stress that the service of the Public Security Centre confirms that for signing in and signing out, that Ckalja's friend signed off at this service on the 28th of July, 1992, because he was leaving for Germany. And I think the number of the next exhibit is 1/57A and B. So I should like to tender that document into evidence, if I have got the number right. Thank you. Could the registrar give me a number for this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, later on did Gruban tell you whether his friend had indeed left the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Ckalja would come by often, and he was surprised on one occasion when he went to visit him and he found some other people in his apartment. He was very surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Why was he surprised?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Because they were very close friends, and that friend of his, that is to say, Ckalja, would often visit that friend of his in that flat. They'd sit around talking for a whole evening. And at that time, if you had some close friends and could stay in their houses, you felt much better.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What was Mr. Gruban's reaction, because his friend had promised to leave him the apartment and didn't?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, he was very surprised and disappointed, because they kept talking about this. His friend always told him that he would leave him his apartment when he left and that he would take care of the apartment, because they were exceptionally close friends, very good friends. And I think they'd known each other for a long time. They had worked for the same company and that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you learn from Gruban whether he ever learnt how this other family came to take up residence in that apartment? You needn't mention their names.

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I think Ckalja told me that the wife of the person living in the apartment showed him a document which had been registered in a court of law on the transactions regarding this apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: And if this contract was registered in a court of law, it can be checked out there, can't it?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, it can. My parents have this kind of contract as well, and I drew up a contract in a court of law with my mother whereby she left her property to me, that kind of property contract.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, did you have occasion to become acquainted with the lady who came to live in Ckalja -- the apartment of Ckalja's friend?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. She has a shop opposite my apartment, and she sells baby food.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to her, how come she came to live there and so on? Did you find out those facts about her?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. We talked, and she told me that they did her a favour, because they helped his sister leave through the International Red Cross and that they did the same to help Ckalja's friend. And as his sister told him that she had left Banja Luka through the International Red Cross, she had managed to leave Republika Srpska, in that same way, Ckalja's friend was able to leave as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did Ckalja tell you about an individual who helped his friend to swap apartments?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: And who was that friend? What was the friend's name? Give us their name, please.

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, let me just think for a moment, please. I can't remember it just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was it somebody that worked in the same company?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. He worked in the same company with Ckalja, and he was a foreman, I think. His name was Kobas Vlado, Vlado Kobas.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was Gruban angry with Kobas for working behind his back?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I can't say. It was logical for it to be Ckalja, if he was his friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, thank you, madam. Let's leave logic for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness. Yes. I'm sorry, I have one further question.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, did your husband, after the second time he went away, did he bring home anything; any valuables, any money, any food, any drink?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: My husband never brought anything home in his life. When he was in uniform, he would carry his cap or his newspaper in his hands, but he would never bring anything home.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did he bring any jewelry home, any gifts of any kind or any money after that second visit?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Absolutely and emphatically no. And in Prijedor, you can go to the jewelry shops. I sold my own earrings and my daughter's. And jewelry, there was no price at all. It was worth very little. All you could do was perhaps buy a drink. And even if you had a wedding band, for example --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Jasminka. I apologise for interrupting, but could the witness switch the other microphone on. We are unable to hear the witness when she turns around. Could both microphones be switched on? The interpreters say that they cannot hear the witness properly because she is not speaking in the direction of the microphone. So that is a technical matter that needs to be resolved. Either switch both microphones on or have the microphone changed. Thank you, and I apologise for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, I just have a short question. Did your husband, from that help, did he receive any counter-assistance from Ckalja or Ckalja's friend, any counter-favours?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Krstan Simic. Who is going to cross-examine the witness? Ms. Somers? Ms. Somers, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I wish to inquire of the Court, if we take the 11.00 break, would it be possible perhaps to break a few minutes earlier to enable me to check something that is not with me? If it's not going to inconvenience the Court, I would like to be able to have something at my disposal and I don't have it here. So perhaps at quarter to or ten to, if that would not be an imposition on the Court or counsel. I'm prepared to begin, certainly, but I'd just like to be able to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is to say, Ms. Somers, you are ready to proceed but you're not ready to finish.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: That's correct. I'd like to have an opportunity just to get something that I thought I had with me and do not. But I'm certainly prepared to start. If the Chamber would just indulge us with perhaps a slightly earlier time period for the break, I'd be grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, very well. We will have our break at around a quarter to eleven. But you can now proceed with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, how many times had you been to the home of this individual, this friend of Ckalja's?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: How many times had you been to the home of the sister of this friend of Ckalja's about whose treasures, jewels, and money --

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did your husband tell you that when they went to the home of the sister of Ckalja's friend that the house had been burned?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, he told me that. That is why her brother couldn't find his way around; that is why he couldn't find it on the first day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What had Ckalja told you that he might have done to have prevented the destruction of the house of such an allegedly good friend? Why was Ckalja surprised?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Simic, what do you object to?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, he was a mechanic, a reserve policeman from the Omarska Police Station Department, and the house was in a different area, so I don't see any link between the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, but my learned counsel opposite is testifying, and I think that that is perhaps something that should be reserved for re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Mr. Simic, it is quite true, you cannot testify instead of the witness. I hope you understand that. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do, Your Honour. But this falls completely outside the scope of the examination-in-chief of this rejoinder witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know where Ckalja's friend was and I don't know where his sister's house was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a second. Mr. Simic, why does that fall outside the scope of the examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness didn't speak about the reasons for the destruction of the house of his sister, who destroyed the house and who might have been able to prevent that destruction. She spoke about the fact that those objects were dug out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, you will have an opportunity to address that during your re-examination. As you know, there are two criteria for cross-examination of the Prosecution and of the Defence: The purpose is to clarify the issue but also to check on the credibility of the witness. You have to enable the Prosecutor to carry out her job, and you will have an opportunity to clarify anything you wish to clarify during your re-examination. Ms. Somers, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you socialise at all during the war -- now, we were talking prewar about your relationship with AW and/or his sister. During the war, how much contact did you have with AW or with his sister?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's Ckalja's friend.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I didn't have any contact at all with him, up until the moment when he came to ask for help.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What about your husband? How much contact did he have with AW and/or his sister?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: We met when he came to my apartment, although our two apartment blocks are situated next to each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What was your understanding of why your husband allowed himself to become involved in this particular effort to recover money and jewels from the house of AW's sister? Why would he do this?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: He was not the first man whom we helped. And on that day my husband was unwilling to go; he was not in a good mood. But I asked him to go there and I wanted to go with him because I always wanted to help people, to help my people as much as I could. As I say, he was not the only person whom we helped. There were many others that we helped.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I want to make sure I understand this. You are saying that you want to leave your area of Prijedor, go to another area, to the home of someone whom you did not have any relationship with, in other words, this sister, and do this for what motive? It's unclear why you would involve yourself, why he would involve himself. I'm sorry. Your answer didn't clear that up. Perhaps you can elaborate on that a bit.

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I can elaborate it. He was not the first or the last individual who came to see me personally for help. I said I could ask my husband whether that could be done. Friends of my husband or Mr. Ckalja would do that. For example, the manager of my company came to see me for help, his wife did as well, and many others. The last time I told you that if you had time to see me, I could have clarified a lot of things for you. I apologise for this digression. But, you know, if I came here to Holland, if I didn't have anyone to stay with, if I didn't have anyone to help me out, would you be willing to help me? Because I would be willing to help you if you were in the same difficult situation. It's something that you probably cannot understand. We are the kind of people who are willing to help others. You probably want to say that me and my husband wanted to help him for some particular reason, for some particular favour that we wanted from him, but you cannot understand that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, both you and your husband, when you testified, gave a series of instances of supposedly good treatment and favours toward Muslims. Is there any particular reason why you might have omitted this good deed in your testimony, whether it was direct or cross or redirect, or why your husband might have eliminated or simply not chosen to talk about this particular incident as a good deed done to help a Muslim? Help us understand that, please.

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Let me try and help you. If he had wanted to lie, he wouldn't have mentioned this in his interview; or perhaps why this husband of mine, since according to you he's such a bad person, when he came back from work and found 20 Muslims in his house, why didn't he ask me, "What are these people doing in my house?" Why didn't he object to that? Why didn't he confront me with that? No, he didn't. Those people had to be fed. But he never said anything. He never wanted to take any money or jewels from that Ckalja's friend, and I don't know what this is all about. I'm not interested in that. But that Ckalja's friend should be ashamed because he remembers very well the coffee that we had together, the jokes we told together. He was not the only person who felt at home in my apartment. Why did he come to see me for help? I don't know. Maybe there is something about Kvocka that makes all Muslims to trust him. They were swarming all around him. I had problems because of that. He didn't dare to go to the Sana River to swim there because of that stigma, war criminal, that he had. I'm sorry I have to go at great length to explain this to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Somers, could you please try and streamline these answers of the witness and your questions for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, your husband did not mention this during his examination. This was a point that was brought up later. You indicated that -- you just said, "I don't know what this is all about." Are you suggesting that you were willing to put yourself into a position of going into a territory that had been cleansed of Muslim residents with your husband or to assist your husband in going into that territory, when your husband, a police officer, spent a good deal of his cross-examination and his defence case suggesting that any risk he took on behalf of Muslims worked against him in his career? Why suddenly in early 1993 would he be willing to take a risk, again assisting a Muslim in broad daylight, in uniform, with another policeman? Maybe you could help us get some insight into that.

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I could do that. My husband's sister came from the States; she's married to a Muslim and I cannot now be with her. My brother also came on Friday. He was also here at the Amsterdam airport, but we couldn't see each other because I was on my way here in order to give my testimony. But talking about helping people, did you ever help anyone in your life? You don't know, dear madam, what I did for those people. I'm sorry, I want to finish my sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, madam, I have to remind you that you are here to answer questions put to you by the Prosecutor. You are not here to ask questions of the Prosecutor. I hope that you understand me. So let us try and be efficient. Let us try to complete your testimony. Please be helpful and try to answer in precise terms the questions that are put to you by Madam Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Your Honour. But I cannot speak about what was going on in my husband's mind on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Kvocka, I haven't asked you anything, I didn't ask any question of you. All I'm telling you is that you have to answer questions put to you by Ms. Somers. Ms. Somers, please try to ask very brief, clear, and concise questions so that Mrs. Jasminka Kvocka can answer your questions in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Ms. Kvocka, why would your husband be willing to take a risk to help a Muslim in early 1993 when it was his and your position that taking such risks as he alleged himself to have done while in Omarska camp could have cost him his career? What changed? Explain that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I really don't understand what this is --

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. A moment ago, a conclusion was requested. I have to remind my learned colleague that Mr. Kvocka was dismissed. He was discharged from his function in Omarska because he had brought parcels, because he had brought a copy of Koran there. This is not the first time that we are hearing allegations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, we are not hearing any allegations or conclusions here. If there has been evidence led to that effect, we will see. I don't know if you have anything to say to the witness at this point, Mr. Simic. No, you don't. The Prosecutor has asked a question concerning an event which happened in 1993, something that we have already discussed, and the witness will -- has supplied us with her answers as best as she could, and one of her answers was that she didn't know. If the witness doesn't know, she is free to say that. Please let the witness answer the questions. Ms. Somers, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, you have not answered my question. Do you remember the question?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember the question. I don't understand the question. I don't know what you want from me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I want you to tell me, Mrs. Kvocka, why it was any less risky for your husband's career in 1993, at the time of this incident that we're talking about with Witness AW, than it would have been in 1992 to help a Muslim? Why was he willing to take this risk to help a Muslim who was no longer a member of the police department, having been cleansed out? Explain that. Why?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Because that's the kind of man he was. He helped everyone he was able to help.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, this individual, did he tell you -- did AW tell you that he was planning to leave the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Was he going to leave the Prijedor area? Did you know about it at the time? At the time this happened, did you know about it?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: That Ckalja's friend --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you know that his sister was going to also leave the territory of Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: He told me that she had already left.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If they left, there would have been no possibility of finding this treasure or money; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: He said that he would call her on the phone so that she could explain him where exactly it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, wasn't the reason that your husband and Gruban, Ckalja, undertook this at that time was because they needed to know where this money was before these people left the territory? Isn't that correct, Mrs. Kvocka? It was for the money for themselves.

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. That Ckalja's friend wanted to know where it was. He was the one who wanted to find it, with their help, because he didn't dare go there alone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, why is it that this is on the eve of the departure of these people? Why not in October 1992, November 1992? Why at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't know. You should ask this man. He was available to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, how many times has your husband gone to dig up the treasure of Muslims who were cleansed out of the area? Please tell us that.

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: On that occasion, but Ckalja came to ask him about his friend, when Ckalja came with his friend of his, and it was upon my insistence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you insist on helping this person, whom you claim not to have known very well, when you found that he was no longer able to remain in Prijedor but was taken to detention centres? Did you offer assistance when he was in detention centres?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Simic. What is your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness was not in a detention centre. She didn't speak about that. She said that she had first come to know him after the first visit to the place to dig up the jewelry. She didn't know the person, so she's not in a position to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the testimony was that the individual had been detained, and my question, of course, to the witness is: During that period when assistance may have been rendered, was any rendered?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please ask your question, Ms. Somers. Mr. Krstan Simic, you will have an opportunity to put additional questions to the witness. Please let us hear your question, Ms. Somers, and it will be the last question before the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Ms. Kvocka, what efforts did you learn about or did you participate in, along with your husband, perhaps, to assist AW, Ckalja's friend, during the period of time of his detention?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't know that he was in detention.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would this be an appropriate time for the break, Your Honour? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but let us first have the witness escorted out of the courtroom, please. We will have a half-hour break at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated. Could the usher please bring in the witness. Ms. Somers, let us continue and let us try to finish the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, you mentioned during the direct examination of this rejoinder testimony that you sold earrings, your own and your daughter's. You sold them, did you not, because they had some value, some value; is that correct? Some value; yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No value at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Then why did you sell them?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, because I had to buy something else of equally small value, but in those days, the gold was practically worthless. And because I didn't work, my husband didn't work, I had to have some money, some cash. And I think that one gram of gold was of very little value in those days.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: But many grams of gold or many items of gold could have had some value, depending on where they were to be sold or traded; isn't that correct? Depending on where they could be sold or traded?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: But probably if people had a lot of gold, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And people who were very wealthy from the areas, the area in which the sister of Ckalja's friend, AW, was living, those were very wealthy people, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't know the area in question, but the people who were very wealthy, they had sent their family and their possessions outside Republika Srpska a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: How do you know that, Mrs. Kvocka?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Many of my friends left in the same manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did your husband assist any of your friends in digging up their valuables from their yards or from hidden places in their homes? Your friends.

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. No, except for this Ckalja's friend.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And this sister of Ckalja's friend you didn't even know, did you?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You thought that she had already left for a third country at the time of this, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's what he told me. That's what her brother said, that he would call her on the phone in a third country.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Well, if other people who left for third countries had already taken their jewels, as you just suggested a minute ago, why do you think that this person would not have done the very same thing if you thought she had left for a third country?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I didn't think that she had left. It was her brother who told us that she had left, but maybe she didn't trust anyone else to go and pick it up.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did it seem odd to you that she would entrust these jewels or money to Gruban, to Ckalja?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, because they were very good friends.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Why did you decide to intervene on behalf of someone whom you did not know, this woman, at this point in time? What motivated you to make good on your debt to Ckalja at this moment in time?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Because he asked me for help.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What was the favour you were repaying, please?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I told my husband to be there with Ckalja, to help him and his friend, because Ckalja had helped me when my husband left Omarska. It was through Ckalja that I was able to send things to my brothers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Why did Ckalja ask you for help in a venture where you didn't know the parties? Why would he ask you? Why would you get involved?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: He knew he could rely on me because I had relied on him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Exactly what did he do for your husband or for you when your husband left Omarska? What was the favour you were repaying?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: It was through him that I was able to send things over to my brothers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And how often did you use his services to do that?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't know. As often as I could, when I had something to send them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did he tell you that he was doing so at risk to himself?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Everybody was doing that as a risk for themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Somers, let me just remind you that the cross-examination time has already elapsed, so if you would please move to the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You mentioned -- I'm sorry, your husband mentioned in his testimony about assisting relatives of yours in the village Alisici - I hope I'm pronouncing it correctly - Alisici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And on page 706 of the transcript - I believe it's the transcript; it could be the LiveNote but I think it's the transcript - he indicated that in order to have vehicles to do that, he abused his official position and got vehicles to do so. Do you recall that? Do you recall that he abused his position and got vehicles to go and help your relatives?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you recall also that your husband had access to, used and abused his official vehicle to ferry your brothers back and forth between Omarska and places outside Omarska during the time of their detention?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was never any mention about any abuse of a vehicle, ferrying back and forth. My learned colleague is now trying to qualify certain behaviour. He did use a vehicle while he was in Omarska. He issued it, but he wasn't abusing that in any way, nor was there any discussion to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the course of its closing arguments, there will be -- we will draw on the documentary evidence to indicate there was an order forbidding the use of vehicles for anything other than official purposes. But I will move on, if I may. Is it okay to proceed, Your Honour? May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I was waiting for the interpretation to hear what you were going to say. But, yes, I think that there has been a certain description or qualification in your question which I think calls for reformulation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I will not go back about the use of the Mercedes for the brothers. I will simply confirm that Mr. Kvocka said that, "In fact, I abused my official position there to avail myself of a vehicle in connection with Alisici," and that was confirmed by this particular witness. And I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please continue, and please try to finish it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: There was a law or a decree in effect, was there not, prohibiting looting and pillaging from the homes of those persons who had fled? There was a law in effect, and your husband, as a police officer, would have had to acknowledge that law, would he not? As would you. Looting/pillaging was prohibited; correct?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Is it not correct that the only activity related to a garage in connection with this entire incident was the distribution of the jewelry that was done in secrecy because it was illegal to do it? The distribution of the jewelry was the only activity that took place in a garage, whoever's garage.

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: This Ckalja's friend -- and by the way, I am not familiar with laws. My husband is aware of that; I am not. But this Ckalja's friend should be ashamed because he was the one who came to see us for help. As for the distribution of that, he didn't have anything to distribute. It was all worthless. My husband, while he was in uniform, never brought a loaf of bread home, let alone anything more valuable. I think that during these past four years you were able to observe the character of my husband. When he was in uniform, all he could bring home was either his cap or a loaf of bread -- or a newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mrs. Kvocka, my last question to you: Were you in the garage when the valuables were distributed? Were you there?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you see them?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, no. No, I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krstan Simic, any additional questions? If yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Kvocka, you mentioned gold and the price that gold was selling for. Can you remember how much a gram of gold was worth?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I think it was somewhere below 3 German marks. Perhaps even less.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Ms. Somers asked you about the garage, whether you -- does this garage exist at all?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I have no idea. There are some garages at Pecani settlement, but who they belong to, I don't know. And I was never in any garage there.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Does your husband know whose these garages were and whether they exist?

utterances.speaker: JASMINKA KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. You can ask him whether he knows which garage belongs to whom.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: It was asked already. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, very well. Judge Fouad Riad, any questions? No. Madam Judge Wald? None. Madam Jasminka Kvocka, you have completed your testimony here. We should like to thank you once again. I'm going to ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krstan Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence will continue its examination of Mr. Miroslav Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krstan Simic, I have a question for you. You have two witnesses. Is there a reason for choosing the order that you chose for the hearing of evidence from the witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But do you realise that we have Rule 90(C) on this subject?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, very well. As you can see -- that is to say, we're now going to hear the testimony of Mr. Kvocka. But he was present during the testimony of the other witness, and that is why I brought Rule 90(C) up. It might have been better for you to have called Mr. Miroslav Kvocka first, but the Rules do not prevent us from hearing Mr. Kvocka now. So I address myself to Mr. Kvocka and the security guards: Could you help Mr. Kvocka move to the witness box?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm going to ask Mr. Kvocka something quite different. I'm not going to go into the same matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Krstan Simic, I understood that you were not going to ask about the same things. But are we addressing ourselves to the same facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, and we're talking about the credibility of Witness AW.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, very well. Mr. Kvocka, I think that you have understood the position. You will continue your testimony under solemn declaration, under the oath you took. May I remind you of that. Thank you. You may be seated. You will now be answering questions put to you by Mr. Simic. Mr. Krstan Simic, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kvocka, during your testimony -- that is to say, during the testimony of Witness AW, Witness AW said that after he completed his military service he became the komandir of the reserve police station. I should like to ask you how one becomes a komandir of a police station, commanding officer.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: That was one of the grossest lies he put forward during his testimony, and I reacted to that and was cautioned by Their Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kvocka, you have been here for a long time. You cannot speak about a testimony in that way, regardless of what the testimony was that was made here. So please abstain from answering in that manner. We don't accept conduct of this kind from the attorneys either, from the counsel either. You are not here to judge the testimony of individuals who have testified. Having said that, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I apologise once again to the Court, and I also wanted to apologise for my previous conduct. As far as the question of how one becomes a leader or komandir, there was no theory under which a metalworker could have become a komandir. You have to have a university degree and all the respect, wield respect and so on. And thousands of people hold university degrees but cannot aspire to becoming a komandir. So it's ludicrous to think that he could have been a komandir or leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka, this was a young man who had just completed his military service. Under such circumstances, was there any chance of him becoming a komandir with all the competencies and authorities that that post has?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, precisely so. Everything speaks to the fact that he could never have become a komandir, especially in the active force and in the reserve force either. And even the reserve officers had university degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka, the witness, during his testimony, also said -- that is to say you yourself said that you didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: But he said that he knew you because you were together at meetings, attended meetings together. Were you in fact at those meetings?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. We were never together at meetings nor could we have been. I did not know him and it was impossible for us to have attended the same meetings. As I said, I knew most of the active policemen, and he was quite certainly not an active policeman. If he was a reserve police officer, then he wasn't in the same police station as myself and it was absolutely impossible for us to have attended the same meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: So you state that he was never a professional policeman as he testified. He said that during 1991, he was.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: I am 100 per cent certain that he wasn't. I have already said that in answer to Ms. Somers' question and I stand by that. Up to 1996, 1997, that is to say 1996, when I stopped working, until I was arrested, he was not an active-duty policeman, right back from 1976 when I began. That is to say, over the past 25 years, he was quite certainly not an active-duty policeman in the Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Why would Witness AW state that he was a komandir and that he was a professional policeman? What would have his motives been to make those assertions?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV KVOCKA [Recalled]
utterances.text: It is difficult for me to say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Go ahead. Mr. Krstan Simic, just a moment, please. Have you got a response to Ms. Somers' objection? Your response, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My response is clear: The witness said he was the komandir of a reserve police station and that he later on become an active-duty policeman and ceased working in the Ljubija mine. That was the testimony from the witness, and I wanted to establish what the motive was, just like my learned friend asked the motive of Mrs. Kvocka to assist and help a moment ago. My question was along those lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.
