utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence calls Witness Ranka Stanar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, madam. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you please read the solemn declaration the usher is giving you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for coming to the Tribunal. You will first answer questions that will be put to you by Mr. Jovan Simic. Mr. Simic, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please tell us your name and surname.

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: My name is Ranka Stanar.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: When and where were you born?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: I was born on the 8th of September, 1959, in the Slavicka opstina Miljanka.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know Dragoljub Prcac?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: Yes. I've known him for 20 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us something about the period of time when the Omarska Investigation Centre was functioning? Do you remember if anything was talked about Mr. Prcac in your village during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: During that period of time, people spoke about Dragoljub as a man who was helping Muslims a lot, and in those days he was not well liked by the Serb population that lived there. At one point in time, there was also rumours that he, probably wishing to help someone, was prepared to point -- pull a pistol on one of the guards. So he wasn't well liked in those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: What is your opinion about Mr. Prcac? What do you think what kind of man he is?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: I told you that I have known Dragoljub for 20 years. Dragoljub is a wonderful person, very kind, sincere, and honest person, and I really can't find words to describe him in a positive sense as much as I would want to.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Waidyaratne?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Ms. Stanar, in 1992, where did you reside?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: In Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Were you neighbours of Mr. Prcac or how did you know Mr. Prcac?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: I was his neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Could you tell us who lived in Mr. Prcac's house during 1992, in the months of May, June, and July?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: In May and June, his mother lived in his house, together with Dragoljub.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And where did Mr. Prcac's family live? Do you know as to where Mr. Prcac's family lived?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: Mr. Prcac has two sons, and they lived in Prijedor. They were in school there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And Mrs. Prcac, too; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: Mrs. Prcac would spend some time with her children and from time to time she was with him and his mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And Mr. Prcac was living in Omarska with his mother; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: Yes. And he would occasionally go to Prijedor to see his wife and children, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: But Mr. Prcac would occasionally go to Prijedor to see his wife and children, if necessary. That's what you say?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My learned friend keeps repeating the same questions. We have heard this question for the second or the third time. His questions are identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I repeated what the witness said, Your Honour. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Waidyaratne, but it is not necessary to repeat what the witness has already said. Please move on with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have other things on our agenda. Let's waste no more time. Please ask your question and do not oblige the witness to repeat her answers, in order to save time, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I will move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mrs. Stanar, you spoke about, say, rumours. From whom did you hear these rumours?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: Omarska is a very small place; people talk. And those rumours were spread by people such as guards or cooks who moved around the investigation centre, and those rumours circulated and it was common knowledge in those days. It's a very small village and people talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you said that Mr. Prcac -- you heard rumours that Mr. Prcac helped Muslims. Do you know any of the Muslims he helped? Did you hear?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: No. I don't know any of the Muslims who were helped by Mr. Prcac, but I do know that there were many such people. And I myself also helped people in those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So it was nothing unusual to you, is that your position?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: It was not unusual, but it was prohibited.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, after you heard these rumours, did you stop associating with the Prcac family, specifically Mr. Prcac, as he was helping the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: No. No. Dragoljub has a big heart and that is how I know him. It is no wonder that he helped Muslims. He would have helped Serbs and Croats. That's the kind of man he is and the way he was brought up, and such was also the society we lived in. It was based on brotherhood and unity.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you question Mr. Prcac at any time after you heard these rumours? Did you ask Mr. Prcac about these rumours?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: No, I did not ask him, because - and I'm telling you my personal opinion - because I believe that it was just something that was done on the spur of the moment because he wanted to achieve something and not that he wanted to do anyone any harm.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, did Mr. Prcac live in Omarska right throughout the conflict and after the conflict, in the same house?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: His family, the two sons and also his wife, also came to stay with him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: His wife lived with him, and their sons were in Prijedor. One was in school; the other was employed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That concludes my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jovan Simic?

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no further questions for the witness. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Judge Fouad Riad? Madam Judge Wald?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Ms. Stanar, besides Mr. Prcac, were there any other guards you heard rumours or talk about being helpful to the Muslims in the Omarska camp? You don't have to name their names, but were there other guards that you would hear that kind of talk or rumour about?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: That they were ready -- I didn't hear those rumours.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat that part of her answer, please.

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: I don't know how well-acquainted you are with the situation and circumstances in our country, but nobody was ready for all that. It came as a surprise to all of us. We were all taken by surprise. And I think that 90 per cent of the population were ready to help as much as they could, to help things. And so the guards, too, if they knew somebody, they would be ready too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I understand your answer, but in your original testimony, you came to tell us that in the village where you were that there were -- that it was said about him that he was helping the Muslims and that the Serbs didn't - I wrote this down - that Serbs didn't like him or didn't like that and that there was a rumour that he pulled a pistol on one of the guards. What I was asking, that sounds as though the rumours were not good ones about him from the point of view of the people who were spreading them, and I wondered if that was true only of him or if there were other guards at Omarska camp you would hear the same kind of thing about, criticism, in other words, that he was helping the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. There were people -- other people who were criticised except Dragoljub Prcac. There was Miroslav Kvocka, for example. Miroslav, too, was in a very difficult situation. He was criticised. And because his good qualities, he was very similar to Dragoljub. They weren't different with all their good qualities, and he, too, was criticised, and he was threatened, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: And there were others without -- there were others. Is that what your testimony was, there were others, too, or are those the only two that you know about?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: Those two I know for sure about. And other people who succeeded in bringing things in, if they heard about people helping, it didn't lead to a scandal. But Miroslav, unfortunately, was exposed to rumours of that kind because he was married to a Muslim, and Dragoljub was criticised because he had pulled a pistol on a guard and he didn't want to stop people from helping other people. That's how I understood it and how I heard it from others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Madam Judge Wald. Mrs. Stanar, do you know if either Mr. Kvocka or Mr. Prcac suffered any consequences due to the fact that they helped Muslims? Did they suffer the consequences of that?

utterances.speaker: Ranka Stanar
utterances.text: As far as Dragoljub is concerned, I think that the greatest consequence was that his son -- the result was that his son was sent to the front. As far as Miroslav, too, by shutting him up in the investigation centre. Although I don't understand their assignments and things, but I do know that he had to go to the battlefield as well and leave his family. So that kind of thing, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. We have no more questions for you, Mrs. Stanar. We would like to thank you for coming. I'm going to ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Jovan Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, our last witness, Radmila Rosic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mrs. Radmila. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are now going to read the solemn declaration handed to you by the usher, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated. Thank you for having come. You are going to answer questions put to you by Mr. Jovan Simic to begin with. Mr. Jovan Simic, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: For the record, could you state your name and surname, please, and your date of birth and place of birth.

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Radmila Rosic. The 13th of February, 1954, at Donja Lamovita.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Rosic, do you know Dragoljub Prcac?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war conflicts in the Prijedor municipality, and we're talking about the month of May onwards, do you know whether Drago was mobilised; and if so, where he was assigned to?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: He was a retired person. He was then mobilised. As I work in the Poljopromet company, we have a lot of outlets, shops and we have burglaries often, and he would go to the crime scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Where was he assigned? To the police station department; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: My next question is the following: Can you remember whether there were any rumours going around about Dragoljub Prcac during the investigation centre of Omarska?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, and not very nice things were said because he helped Muslims. People even said that he had pulled a gun at one of the guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Knowing Dragoljub Prcac, what could you tell us about him as a man, as an individual, human being?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: He was quiet and calm, a good person, a good man. He did a lot of farming; kept his mother and his two sons who are invalids, provided for them. I also know that he had some pigs. I would pass by his plot of land frequently. He had sheep and pigs.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Mrs. Rosic, did you know a person by the name of Krle, Milojica Kos?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you provide a statement for Mr. Kos?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Do you remember what you said in that statement?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: That I have known him since childhood. We were born in the same place. And he carried some things, he helped.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Well, did you ask Mr. Kos to carry anything to the camp? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Not me personally. But some people did, some of my female colleagues did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So Mr. Kos took things to the camp; is that your position?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And you said that you didn't hear good things about -- I'm sorry. What is your answer to my earlier question? My question was: "So Mr. Kos took things to the camp; is that your position?" What is your answer?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: So now you said that you heard bad things about Mr. Prcac, saying that he took things to the camp for the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jovan Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that is not what the witness said. The witness said that she heard he had helped the Muslims, not that he took things.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Very well. I'm sorry, Your Honour, if I -- I would ask this question:

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: What did you hear, these bad things about Mr. Prcac?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: That he helped the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: How? Did you hear as to how he helped the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You don't know as to how Mr. Prcac helped the Muslims in the camp.

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Now, did you hear rumours about Mr. Kos, bad things about him?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Prcac during 1992, in the months of May, June, and July?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Only when he went to investigate the scene of the crime with my colleague, Bogdan Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did he come to the company that you worked to investigate any things during that time?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: You don't know as to what exactly Mr. Prcac was assigned during the months of June and July?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Did you know that Mr. Prcac worked in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jovan Simic, any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just briefly, Your Honour, a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rosic, the company you worked for, how many shops and outlets did it have in Omarska, in the territory of Omarska?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: It has about 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did it have any warehouses?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many shops and warehouses were burgled, and whether some of those facilities were burgled several times in a row?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: They were burgled daily, some of them several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if your firm could file a request with the insurance company for compensation without the police doing an on-the-spot investigation?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt my learned friend, Your Honour, but I don't see the relevance with regard to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You don't see it, Mr. Waidyaratne? Okay. Mr. Jovan Simic, perhaps you could respond and enlighten us.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My learned colleague has attempted to show that the witness does not know what he did, and I am now challenging that by showing that an on-site investigation had to be conducted and that Mr. Prcac was present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, very well. Please proceed, Mr. Jovan Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: My question was: Could you file a request with the insurance company for compensation without the police investigating the crime scene and compiling a report?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: No, we were not able to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. This didn't come up in cross-examination and I do not see how Mr. Simic could re-examine this witness on these issues, new areas of evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ask your question, Mr. Jovan Simic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Once again, you had to have an on-the-spot police investigation for you to be able to make claims to the insurance company. Now, in this report, was the report signed and the investigation conducted by Mr. Prcac?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you see the accountant in the company?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you have to make a list of what was stolen, destroyed, and so on, in order to receive compensation?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Waidyaratne.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: Objection again, Your Honour. This didn't transpire in cross-examination. These are new areas, and I do not know how this witness could testify with regard to what Mr. Prcac did with the investigation. She would have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAIDYARATNE
utterances.text: And Mr. Simic is testifying. He's giving --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There perhaps you have a point. I'm going to ask Mr. Jovan Simic to ask questions without leading the witness. But you can continue to ask your question, Mr. Simic. So you can finish off your question, complete your questions, but ask them in a direct manner and not in a leading way, please. Do you understand what I'm saying when I am saying "ask a direct question"? What I mean is don't lead the witness. Ask your question so that you are not leading the witness. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Rosic, did you have a document of that kind, that is to say, the minutes or a record or report signed by Dragoljub Prcac, in your hands?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was the document signed by anybody else; and if so, by whom?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Bosko Davic and Rade Andzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: And my last question: The rumours about him drawing a gun, that rumour, was it connected with the investigation centre of Omarska or the village of Omarska?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: The investigation centre of Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Fouad Riad, any questions? No. Madam Judge Wald?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I have one question, Ms. Rosic. In the months of May and June 1992, how often did you see Mr. Prcac in your line of work? I mean you said that there were these many outlets and he would be involved in the crime investigations of it. Can you remember how many times you saw him in that line of work during those months, approximately?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Well, several sometimes. I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Were some of those times in May and some in June or were they all in June or all in May? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Madam Judge Wald. Mrs. Rosic, you have told us that there were rumours. Can you repeat for us what exactly you heard, the actual words? What were people saying exactly?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: They were saying that he was helping the Muslims a lot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only that?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Only that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What did people understand by that? Where was the problem?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Very well. How many times did you hear rumours of that kind bandied about?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Well, two or three times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two or three times, you say. Was there any difference in the rumours when you heard them once or the second time or the third time or did people always say the same thing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Generally speaking, that was it. It was about his helping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Where did you hear those rumours? Where were you when you heard that?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Well, I work a great deal after working hours, accountancy and so forth. I work in the cafes and I do part-time work and that's where I heard these rumours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but where? Tell us one occasion when you heard -- you said you heard rumours two or three times. Where did you hear this rumour once, on one occasion? Give us an example of one occasion, or don't you remember?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Do you happen to remember the person who told you that, who you heard it from?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you don't know the name or you don't know the person? Which is it of those two?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know the person or the name of the person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you don't know the person or their name on the two or three occasions when you heard the rumour; is that right? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't one person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. How many people said that?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Okay. No problem. If I understand you correctly, you're saying that you don't remember who told you. You do, however, remember that you heard these rumours on two or three occasions, and you tell us that there were more than one person who's talked about these things; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADMILA ROSIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. We have no more questions for you, Mrs. Rosic. We should like to thank you for having come, and we wish you bon voyage back to your place of residence and work. I'm going to ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jovan Simic, I think this brings us to your last witness for the day, is that right, or in general?

utterances.speaker: MR. J. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right, Your Honour. It is the last Defence witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We still have to decide on the documents, and we're going to leave the issue of documents and tendering into evidence the ones that Mr. Krstan Simic wished to tender when we come to discuss the entirety of the documents that the Chamber is going to consider. We have a number of outstanding documents to consider. I can't tell you now when you will have a ruling by the Chamber, but perhaps tomorrow. I think the Chamber might have a ruling for you tomorrow. So we'll include to the initial batch the ones that Mr. Simic tendered, and we'll set a deadline for the Defence to answer any additional questions which the Chamber might need to clarify in order to make a ruling on the documents. There are documents where the Chamber can make a definitive decision; there are others where we need some more details. So we'll set a date, a deadline for response by the parties, additional filings, of about seven days, but we're going to include the documents put forward today by Mr. Krstan Simic, and we'll have a ruling in due course. As to the other matters, we are going to stick to our schedule; that is to say that we're going to meet again. I can't tell you off the bat by heart, but I think that it will be -- have you got the calendar, Madam Registrar? Can you help us, please? No? I think the parties are well aware of the dates. 13th of July [as interpreted]? Thank you. There's another question that I have -- that I would like to address, and that is the following: We have granted one week for oral arguments and a day and a half to the Prosecution so that the three and a half days remain for the Defence to use in proportion unless the Defence has a proposal to make. So for the moment, the Chamber has received no additional proposals from the Defence, which means that the three and a half days will be divided up equally for each of the Defence counsel, the Defence teams, and that is how we shall proceed. I don't know if anybody would like to make any observations with respect to that matter before we close our business for today. Would the Prosecution like to make any observations in that regard perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Not at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. The Defence counsels? I see Mr. Fila on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not the 13th of July, the 16th of July. That was an error in the transcript. I said the 16th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, could you take a look at the calendar and tell us the exact date, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is the 16th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It is indeed the 16th of July. There we have it. I wish you every success in your work until we meet in the courtroom again. Until then, I adjourn the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 16th day of July, 2001, at 9.20 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.00 p.m.,
